The broad backdrop is mixed and choppy rather than cleanly directional: funding sits in a neutral regime, open interest is contracting, and crowd positioning leans modestly short overall. That context matters because the ranking reads best as a research-priority queue, not as an execution-ready board.

Ranked queue:
1. SKHX is the highest-priority name for deeper review, but it is leading because the anomaly is loud, not because the setup is clean. It posted the strongest anomaly score (91.18) and final score (74.15), with a bearish tilt driven by deeply positive funding (0.060622%) and long-leaning long/short ratios at 4h (3.8473) and 1h (2.3898). That combination points to crowding risk. The key downgrade is confirmation quality: spot confirmation is missing, activity-supported confirmation was unavailable, the 24h long/short liquidation pressure imbalance reads balanced, and current heatmap pressure was unavailable. In plain terms, SKHX deserves first review because it may be overextended, but it still needs cleaner directional proof before the read improves.

2. KAS is the cleaner second-pass candidate. Its spot confirmation is confirmed, but the perp structure is still neutral, so the case is more about potential development than present conviction. The main signals are 24h open-interest contraction of -16.03%, alignment in open-interest behavior across 4h and 24h, and a 24h long/short liquidation pressure imbalance that is heavily long-side dominated (153578.89 versus 231.31). Current heatmap pressure is stronger above the market than below, with the top upside pressure scores near 0.031818 and 0.032214, versus downside pressure near 0.03045 and 0.030162. That makes KAS a better-confirmed name than SKHX, but still one waiting for the perp structure to become more decisive.

3. 1000BONK also sits in the monitor bucket rather than a stronger tier. Spot confirmation is confirmed and strengthened, but the perp structure remains neutral. Its signal mix includes 24h open-interest contraction of -19.11%, a 1h short-leaning long/short ratio of 0.5853, and a strong 24h long-side liquidation pressure imbalance (1069059.8 versus 76956.1). Current heatmap pressure is again more concentrated above the market, with top upside pressure near 0.0058285 and 0.005881, compared with downside pressure near 0.0053335 and 0.005221. The takeaway is similar to KAS: the name has enough evidence to stay near the front of the queue, but not enough structure yet to move beyond monitoring.

4. CAKE is notable because it is the clearest bullish-leaning name inside the top five, even though it only ranks fourth. Spot confirmation is confirmed with spot inflow, and the long/short ratio is short-leaning on both 24h (0.5833) and 1h (0.5743), creating bullish multi-timeframe resonance. Even so, the perp structure is still neutral, and the 24h long/short liquidation pressure imbalance remains long-side dominated (108413.31 versus 489.48), which keeps squeeze-and-unwind risk in play. Current heatmap pressure is stronger above the market, with top upside pressure near 1.44555 and 1.40525, while downside pressure clusters near 1.3045 and 1.31535. CAKE is therefore interesting less as a finished setup and more as a name that could improve quickly if the structure firms up.

5. ETHFI rounds out the ranked list with a neutral profile. Spot confirmation is confirmed, but the setup still lacks a stronger directional handoff. Its main inputs are 24h open-interest contraction of -11.91%, a 4h short-leaning long/short ratio of 0.5888, and a 24h long-side liquidation pressure imbalance of 345608.49 versus 122136.74. Current heatmap pressure is strongest above the market near 0.3722 and 0.3974, with downside pressure near 0.35825 and 0.36185. ETHFI remains valid for review, but it does not yet outrank KAS or 1000BONK on setup quality.

Secondary candidates still matter. ALLO is the most interesting backup on the bullish side, with 24h open interest up 84.64%, alignment across 1h, 4h, and 24h, and short-side liquidation pressure dominance, but it stayed outside the final top five. BSB and EDEN are the more bearish secondary names, both driven by 24h open-interest contraction greater than 22%, aligned multi-timeframe open-interest behavior, and materially stronger long-side liquidation pressure. If the primary queue loses quality on re-check, ALLO is the best upside follow-up, while BSB and EDEN are the more defensive bearish backups.

The main review priority is confirmation quality. Confidence is only medium because spot confirmation is incomplete for at least one top setup, and that missing confirmation belongs to the highest-ranked name. Coverage elsewhere is usable: market snapshots were available, perp structure projection covered all five ranked names, and spot confirmation was confirmed on four of the five. The practical read is straightforward: keep SKHX at the top of the review queue because its anomaly is strongest, but do not upgrade it until confirmation improves; in the meantime, KAS and 1000BONK may offer better review efficiency because their evidence base is firmer, while CAKE is the most constructive upside monitor if the market stops chopping."},"action_guidance":{"bias":"context_only","reference_action":"SKHX: Keep the name on review but wait for cleaner directional confirmation."}}}},"executionMeta":{"executionTimeMs":"99392"}}
